subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: A problem in calculus is given to two students A and B whose chances of solving it are 1/3 and 1/4 respectively. Find the probability of the problem being solved if both of them try independently.

mark_split.label: Define the events and write P(A), P(B)
Solved = not (both fail); multiply the independent complements

recall_prompt: Say how you would find the probability that the problem is solved — the events, the complements, and why the complements are multiplied.
insider_note: "Solved" means at least one of them solves it. The short route is 1 − P(both fail); the long route P(A) + P(B) − P(A)P(B) gives the same 1/2 and is also accepted.

steps.label: Events and given values
steps.margin_note: First mark. Name the events with the letters the question uses; the problem is "solved" when A ∪ B occurs.

lines.text: Let A, B be the events that the problem is
solved by A and by B respectively. Then

recall.must_convey: That A and B are the events of each student solving the problem, with P(A) = 1/3, P(B) = 1/4, independent.
accept: let A and B be the events that each student solves it with probabilities one third and one fourth independent
A solves with a third, B with a quarter, independently
define the two solving events, 1 by 3 and 1 by 4
A solve chese event, B solve chese event, 1 by 3, 1 by 4, independent

steps.why: The problem is solved if at least one succeeds — the union. Naming the events lets that union be written.
common_mistakes: Not stating that the events are independent, which the product step needs.

steps.label: Complements
steps.margin_note: Second mark. P(Aᶜ) = 1 − 1/3 = 2/3 and P(Bᶜ) = 1 − 1/4 = 3/4: the chances each one fails.

accept: A fails with two thirds and B fails with three quarters
P A complement is 2 by 3 and P B complement is 3 by 4
the complements are two by three and three by four
A fail ayye probability 2 by 3, B 3 by 4

steps.why: "Not solved" means both fail, and each failure is a complement.

steps.label: P(solved) = 1 − P(both fail)
steps.margin_note: Two marks. P(A ∪ B) = 1 − P(Aᶜ ∩ Bᶜ); the complements of independent events are independent, so P(Aᶜ ∩ Bᶜ) = (2/3)(3/4) = 1/2.

lines.text: The problem is solved if at least one solves it:

accept: solved is one minus both fail which is one minus two thirds times three quarters equals half
P of A union B is one minus P A complement times P B complement, one minus half, half
the answer is one by two
solved ante 1 minus both fail, 1 minus 2 by 3 into 3 by 4, half
heard_as: one minus two by three into three by four

steps.why: "At least one" is easier through its opposite "none". The complements are independent because A and B are, so "none" is a product.
common_mistakes: Adding 1/3 + 1/4 = 7/12 and stopping — that double counts both solving.
Multiplying (1/3)(1/4) = 1/12, which is P(both solve), not P(solved).
